scope.note: A national planning level is not a forecast for any one county, city, or utility.

headline: Top Off the Pantry
summary: Elevated background risk. Keep about two weeks of food and water. No panic buying.
supplyWindow: About 2 weeks of food and water
rationale: Level 4 holds. AAA's national average diesel price on November 15 was $6.02 a gallon, down from $6.19 a week earlier but still about 60 percent above $3.77 a year ago, and regular gasoline slipped to $3.82. EIA's latest weekly report, for the week ending November 6, shows distillate stocks at 103.3 million barrels, still 6.8 percent below a year earlier, while Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude fell to 279.5 million barrels; the next weekly report had not been released at review time. Brent settled at $95.84 on November 13 after a second weekly decline as the IEA reported a return to global surplus, but the IEA still describes diesel supply as tight. Fuel stays expensive rather than unavailable. At home, the transportation secretary traced the November 13 nationwide FAA ground stop to a router that flooded air traffic systems during a copper-to-fiber upgrade; more than 5,900 flights were cancelled on November 14 as airlines cleared the backlog, the FAA expects normal schedules by the end of November 15, and officials found no evidence of a cyberattack. Overseas risk did not ease. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a six-drone attack on a U.S. radar at Bahrain's Riffa Air Base on November 15, the second such claim in three days; Bahrain sounded sirens and said it intercepted the attacks, and the U.S. military had not commented. Iran also claimed two more tankers hit mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, claims not independently verified, and the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports continues. These are attacks and claims abroad, not attacks on the United States or an ordered U.S. strike. Russian drones again hit energy sites in Ukraine, talks on Ukraine produced a reported U.S. Donbas-for-NATO idea but no ceasefire, the U.S., Chinese, and Russian leaders plan to meet in Shenzhen on November 19, and Taiwan reported 1 Chinese military aircraft sortie, down from 10. The United States was reported to have lost its measles elimination status, a public health warning rather than a supply disruption. No confirmed disruption of fuel, power, food distribution, or payments across multiple U.S. regions was found. Southeast freeze warnings, a marginal severe storm risk on the Texas Gulf Coast, and western wind and mountain snow advisories are regional and are not averaged into the national number, and no tropical cyclone formation is expected in the next 7 days. Level 3 would need a confirmed multi-region disruption; none was confirmed today.
disclaimer: PANTRYCON is an independent, unofficial household preparedness assessment for the United States. It is not affiliated with the U.S. government or the armed forces. It is not DEFCON, and it is not a civil-defense or military alert. The number is a national planning snapshot. It does not mean every community faces the same immediate threat.
overrides: Follow local official instructions first. Evacuation orders, boil-water notices, shelter-in-place orders, and other location-specific emergency alerts always override this national level.

evidence.title: U.S. distillate fuel oil stocks
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 6 lists distillate fuel oil stocks at 103.3 million barrels for the week ending November 6, 2026, up 4.1 million from 99.3 million the prior week. The year-earlier figure is 110.9 million, so stocks are 6.8 percent below a year ago, compared with 11.0 percent below in the previous report.
evidence.limits: This is a national stock figure for diesel and heating oil at refineries, in pipelines, and at bulk terminals. It is not a count of fuel at neighborhood stations, and it is not an outage report. East Coast (PADD 1) distillate stocks were 23.8 million barrels, up from 22.6, but still 12.2 percent below a year earlier. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) stocks were 43.2 million, up from 40.5.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 6

evidence.title: Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude
evidence.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report Table 1 lists Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude at 279.5 million barrels for the week ending November 6, 2026, down 2.6 million from 282.2 million the prior week. The year-earlier figure on that table is 410.4 million barrels.
evidence.limits: A smaller strategic crude stock is context for the national fuel buffer. It is not, by itself, a household supply emergency, and this page does not turn it into a price forecast.

source.label: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, Table 1

evidence.title: National average retail diesel and gasoline prices
evidence.summary: AAA's national average table on November 15, 2026 lists diesel at $6.0198 a gallon, compared with $6.0366 the day before, $6.1929 a week earlier, $6.3173 a month earlier, and $3.7703 a year earlier. Regular gasoline is listed at $3.8242, down from $4.0203 a week earlier and $4.3344 a month earlier, against $3.0758 a year earlier.
evidence.limits: A retail price average shows cost pressure, not whether fuel is physically available at stations. Diesel is still about 60 percent above its year-ago price.

evidence.title: Delayed weekly petroleum report published
evidence.summary: EIA published the delayed Weekly Petroleum Status Report on November 12, 2026, after the November 11 federal holiday. Table 1 shows commercial crude stocks of 414.4 million barrels, up 4.7 million in the week ending November 6, total motor gasoline stocks of 210.8 million barrels, up 1.8 million and 2.8 percent above a year earlier, and total stocks excluding the strategic reserve up 11.4 million barrels.
evidence.limits: One week of rising stocks does not establish a trend. Commercial crude remains 3.1 percent below a year earlier, and the report does not measure retail station supply.

evidence.title: Global oil supply back above demand, diesel still tight
evidence.summary: The International Energy Agency's Oil Market Report published November 13, 2026 says global oil supply rose by 2.3 million barrels a day to 105.4 million in October, surpassing demand for the first time since the war in Iran began, and that observed inventories rose by 52 million barrels, the first increase since June. It expects a surplus in the fourth quarter but says severe tightness in product supply, especially diesel, remains the overriding concern, and that on-land stocks are at their lowest level since at least 2016.
evidence.limits: A global balance forecast is not a measure of U.S. station supply. The IEA notes that attacks on shipping are a downside risk to the recovery.

evidence.title: Nationwide flight ground stop traced to an air traffic telecom upgrade
evidence.summary: The BBC reported that the four-hour nationwide FAA ground stop that began at 3:54 PM EST on November 13, 2026, the longest since September 2001, was caused by a technical issue during a contractor's copper-to-fiber upgrade of air traffic communications: the Transportation Secretary said a router being worked on began flooding other air traffic control systems. More than 15,000 U.S. flights were delayed or cancelled that day, and more than 5,900 were cancelled and 7,000 delayed on November 14 as airlines cleared the backlog. The FAA said schedules should return to normal by the end of November 15, and its administrator said there was zero evidence of anything nefarious.
evidence.limits: The exact root cause is still under investigation. This disrupted passenger travel and air cargo timing, not fuel, power, or grocery distribution, and it did not change the national level.

evidence.title: Crude oil ends a second straight weekly decline
evidence.summary: Reuters reported that Brent crude futures settled at $95.84 a barrel on November 13, 2026, up 2 cents, and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at $88.56, down 18 cents. Both benchmarks were on track for a weekly drop of about 2.5 percent, after falls of 16 and 13 percent the week before, as traders weighed a growing global supply surplus against continuing risk to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
evidence.limits: Crude prices are a cost signal for fuel, not a measure of U.S. supply on hand.

evidence.title: Nationwide grid emergency
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm an active nationwide electricity emergency from a grid operator or a federal energy office, and did not find a new multi-region U.S. power outage reported on November 14 or 15, 2026. The level is not based on a live outage map.
evidence.limits: A gap in this snapshot is not an all-clear. Local outages can be serious while the national planning level stays at 4.

evidence.title: Microsoft 365 outage blamed on a network change, not an attack
evidence.summary: The BBC reported that a global Microsoft outage that began on the afternoon of November 12, 2026 and continued into November 13 slowed some U.S. and Canadian government, court, train, and hospital services that rely on Microsoft email, while essential and emergency services were not affected. Microsoft said the outage was not caused by a cybersecurity incident, tied it to a technical issue following a recent network change, and said it had addressed the underlying issue and was gradually restoring services.
evidence.limits: This is a business email and collaboration outage, not a reported disruption of fuel, power, food distribution, or payment systems.

evidence.title: Nationwide cyber disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide cyber disruption of U.S. utilities, pipelines, grocery cold chains, or payment systems on November 14 or 15, 2026. Officials said the November 13 flight ground stop was not a cyberattack, and Microsoft said its November 12 to 13 outage was not a cybersecurity incident. Social-media claims were not used.
evidence.limits: A later confirmation from an operator or from CISA could raise the level. Absence from this page is not a finding that nothing happened.

evidence.title: Investigation of August military commissary freezer failures
evidence.summary: Military.com reported on November 12, 2026 that the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, Army investigators, and the Defense Commissary Agency are investigating whether cyberattacks caused refrigeration failures that spoiled frozen food and limited sales to dry goods at commissaries on several U.S. installations in August, and are working with French authorities. A U.S. official described it as an investigation into a suspected cyberattack.
evidence.limits: Investigators have not publicly established the cause or who was responsible, and no group has claimed it. The failures were in August and limited to on-base stores. This is not a report of a current civilian grocery disruption.

evidence.title: France blames Iranian cyber unit for supermarket fridge sabotage
evidence.summary: NPR reported on November 9, 2026 that France's national cybersecurity agency said Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites in France in October, raising temperatures overnight and spoiling food, and also hit several small hydroelectric plants with moderate effects. France linked the Shahid Kaveh unit to Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and Paris prosecutors are seeking international arrest warrants. Grocery stores in other European countries were hit in similar attacks the week before.
evidence.limits: This is an attack in Europe. NPR notes that refrigeration failures at U.S. military commissaries in August have not been officially attributed or confirmed as cyberattacks, and this review found no confirmed attack on U.S. grocery supply.

evidence.title: Federal warning on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers
evidence.summary: On November 5, 2026, CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA, and the Department of Transportation published a fact sheet warning of ongoing cyber threat activity against industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. CISA said actors worldwide are targeting unpatched or internet-exposed temperature and refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage, which could change temperatures and cause loss of inventory, and urged operators to take those devices off the internet and patch them.
evidence.limits: This is a warning and guidance, not a report of a U.S. outage or of spoiled U.S. food supplies.

evidence.title: Southeast freeze warnings, Texas coast storms, and western wind and mountain snow
evidence.summary: This snapshot is not connected to a live National Weather Service or FEMA feed. A check of active NWS alerts early on November 15, 2026 listed freeze warnings across parts of North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, southeastern Virginia, and the Florida Panhandle region; wind advisories in western Washington, Oregon, northern California, and the upper Texas and Louisiana coast; winter weather advisories in the Sierra Nevada and south-central Alaska; a river flood warning in western Washington; and heavy freezing spray warnings off Alaska's Arctic coast. The Storm Prediction Center's day 1 outlook shows a marginal risk of severe thunderstorms along the middle and lower Texas Gulf Coast. These are regional and are not averaged into the national number.
evidence.limits: Weather can change quickly. Local NWS alerts and emergency instructions always take priority over this page.

evidence.title: No tropical cyclones expected
evidence.summary: The National Hurricane Center's Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook issued at 7:00 AM EST on November 15, 2026 says tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days for the North Atlantic, the Caribbean Sea, and the Gulf of America.
evidence.limits: A 7-day outlook is not a guarantee, and it does not cover winter storms, flooding, or wildfire.

source.label: National Hurricane Center, Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook

evidence.title: Nationwide civil disruption
evidence.summary: This review did not confirm a nationwide civil disruption that is stopping household resupply, and found no report that the Insurrection Act had been invoked as of November 15, 2026. A Polymarket prediction market on whether the act is invoked by December 31, 2026 was trading near 5.5 percent yes on November 15. Flight disruptions after the November 13 ground stop are a transportation problem, not civil unrest.
evidence.limits: A betting market price is not a forecast by this project or an official assessment. Civil conditions can change quickly in one place. Local official instructions come first.

source.label: Polymarket, Insurrection Act invoked by December 31

evidence.title: United States loses measles elimination status
evidence.summary: NPR, with KFF Health News, reported on November 14, 2026 that the Pan American Health Organization concluded this week that measles has reestablished regular transmission in the United States, ending the elimination status held since 2000. PAHO planned a public announcement on November 17. NPR cited more than 8,000 people sickened and 13 measles-associated deaths reported by states in outbreaks over the past two years.
evidence.limits: The decision was reported through people with knowledge of the deliberations before the official announcement. It is a public health warning that makes vaccination records worth checking, not a disruption of food, water, power, or fuel.

evidence.title: Iran reports more tankers hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz
evidence.summary: Anadolu Agency reported that Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said early on November 15, 2026 that two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz while using what it called an unauthorized route with tracking systems switched off, after similar claims on November 13 and 14. Al Jazeera reported the Guards also said two other tankers turned back after warnings, and that Iran says the strait remains closed and under its control, which the United States rejects.
evidence.limits: The vessels were not named and casualties were not reported. The claims were not independently verified at the time of this review, and the U.S. military has said it cleared the main routes of mines. These are incidents abroad, not attacks on the United States.

evidence.title: Iran claims a second drone attack on a U.S. radar in Bahrain
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera reported on November 15, 2026 that Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched six drones at a U.S. air defense radar at Bahrain's Riffa Air Base, the second such claim in three days. Bahrain's Interior Ministry sounded sirens and issued two shelter alerts starting about 4:30 AM local time, and the Bahrain Defence Force said its air defenses thwarted several Iranian aerial attacks. The U.S. military had not commented on the November 15 claim. After the November 13 claim, U.S. Central Command said it shot down two Guard drones with no injuries or damage and denied that a radar was hit. The U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in place and talks remain stalled.
evidence.limits: Damage, if any, was not confirmed at the time of this review. This is an attack claim abroad, not an attack on U.S. soil, and it does not report a change in U.S. supplies.

evidence.title: President says no deal with Iran is needed
evidence.summary: The Washington Post reported on November 12, 2026 that the President said the United States does not need a deal with Iran and ended the Vice President's negotiating effort. Reuters, via CNBC, reported that he indicated the naval blockade and sanctions would stay in place.
evidence.limits: A statement on diplomacy is not an ordered attack. It lowers the odds of a near-term deal that would reopen the strait, but it does not report a change in U.S. supplies.

evidence.title: Houthis claim more strikes on Saudi targets
evidence.summary: Investing.com reported on November 14, 2026 that Yemen's Houthis claimed missile strikes targeting Riyadh airport and Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, after claiming attacks on November 12 on a pipeline pumping station, a Yanbu oil facility, and an Aramco building in Riyadh. Saudi authorities had not confirmed those claims.
evidence.limits: These are unconfirmed claims abroad. Saudi Arabia said a November 9 strike on the pipeline did not affect operations.

evidence.title: Attack on Saudi East-West pipeline
evidence.summary: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on November 9, 2026 that the East-West pipeline was targeted in the Madinah region, causing a limited fire that emergency teams put out, with no injuries and pipeline operations unaffected. The pipeline is Saudi Arabia's main route for moving crude to the Red Sea without passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
evidence.limits: The ministry did not name the attacker. This review found no confirmed effect on U.S. fuel supplies.

source.label: Arab News, citing the Saudi energy ministry, Nov 9, 2026

evidence.title: Treasury Secretary moved to a military base after Iranian threats
evidence.summary: CBS News reported on November 11, 2026 that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated from his Washington-area home to a military base following Iranian threats against his life. A Treasury spokesperson said he will not be deterred and remains committed to the sanctions campaign and the naval blockade against Iran.
evidence.limits: The relocation was reported through people familiar with the matter, and the severity of the threats was not made public. A protective move is not an attack and does not report a U.S. supply disruption.

evidence.title: Chinese military activity around Taiwan
evidence.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry reported 1 Chinese military aircraft sortie, 8 navy ships, and 3 official ships operating around Taiwan in the 24 hours ending 6 a.m. local time on November 15, 2026, down from 10 aircraft sorties the day before.
evidence.limits: Routine reported activity, not a blockade or an attack.

source.label: Taiwan Ministry of National Defense, Nov 15, 2026

evidence.title: No ceasefire; U.S. raised a Donbas-for-NATO idea
evidence.summary: The BBC reported on November 14, 2026 that Ukraine's president said U.S. envoys had floated the idea of Ukraine joining NATO if it withdrew from the parts of the Donbas region it still holds, the first time the question had been raised. He said Ukraine is not ready to cede territory but that a full package with security guarantees could be put to a referendum.
evidence.limits: Talks continue. No ceasefire has been agreed, and this is a reported proposal, not a deal.

evidence.title: Russian drones hit Ukrainian energy sites again
evidence.summary: Ukrainska Pravda, citing the Zhytomyr regional military administration, reported that Russian drones struck energy infrastructure and damaged four houses in the Zhytomyr region overnight on November 14 to 15, 2026, with no deaths or injuries reported, and that six people were injured in an attack on Chornomorsk in the Odesa region.
evidence.limits: This is war damage in Ukraine. It shows continuing attacks on energy systems abroad, not a threat to the U.S. grid.

evidence.title: U.S., China, and Russia leaders plan a meeting at APEC
evidence.summary: Anadolu Agency reported that the Kremlin said on November 14, 2026 that the U.S., Chinese, and Russian presidents will hold a trilateral meeting on November 19 in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, after the White House announced it. U.S. officials said nuclear arms reduction and the Middle East war would be discussed, but not Ukraine.
evidence.limits: This is a scheduled meeting, not an outcome. China had not separately confirmed it in the reports reviewed, and expectations for a breakthrough are low.

evidence.title: Drone alerts in the Baltic states and a strike on a Russian warship
evidence.summary: Al Jazeera and Reuters reported on November 13, 2026 that Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania warned citizens to take shelter from drones in their airspace on November 11 and NATO jets were scrambled, during Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia's Leningrad region. Finland's military said it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and that Finland is not under any immediate military threat.
evidence.limits: The origin and details of the warship strike were not confirmed by Finland. No direct NATO-Russia clash was reported.

evidence.title: State Department worldwide caution
evidence.summary: On November 6, 2026, the State Department's TravelGov account warned U.S. citizens abroad of increased threats from Iranian-supported groups, Iranian efforts to target U.S. officials, and possible flight cancellations or airspace closures.
evidence.limits: This is a travel advisory for Americans abroad. It is not an attack order, and it does not report a domestic supply disruption.

source.label: U.S. Department of State, TravelGov, Nov 6, 2026

evidence.title: Defense Department base power resilience plan
evidence.summary: The War Zone reported on October 26, 2026 that under the Defense Department's FORTRESS America initiative, announced September 30, major U.S. military installations are expected to sustain essential operations for at least 90 days without outside electricity, water, fuel, and communications support. Officials have described early work as installation assessments, microgrids, and battery storage. This review found no newer program announcement on November 13 or 14.
evidence.limits: This is a long-term military readiness plan for bases. It is not a warning of a coming public blackout, and it is not this project's level 1 label.

raise: A later EIA or Energy Department report of a physical fuel-distribution failure across more than one region, rather than lower stocks alone.
A verified multi-state electricity emergency long enough to interrupt ordinary food resupply.
A confirmed cyber disruption of pipelines, payment systems, or grid operations with household effects, stated by the operator or by CISA.
Official emergency declarations that restrict movement or commerce across many states at the same time.
Concurrent verified disasters that break national distribution, as distinct from a single local storm.
lower: A later Weekly Petroleum Status Report showing distillate stocks rebuilding toward the prior-year level, without a physical distribution failure.
No verified multi-region outage of power, fuel, food, or payments in the sources reviewed that week.
A return to level 5 when the several-day Ready.gov basic kit is again the matching band, because background fuel tightness is no longer the best reading.

levels.name: Normal Larder
levels.means: Routine conditions. Keep the Ready.gov basic kit: several days of food and water, at about one gallon of water per person per day.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a particular town is free of storms, outages, or local alerts.

levels.name: Top Off the Pantry
levels.means: Elevated background risk without a verified nationwide emergency. Keep about two weeks of food and water at home, which matches the American Red Cross home-kit suggestion.
levels.doesNotMean: It does not mean a shortage is underway, and it is not a call to panic-buy.

levels.name: Deep Pantry
levels.means: A credible near-term disruption of grid, fuel, food distribution, or civil order affecting resupply across multiple regions, confirmed from a primary source.
levels.doesNotMean: A headline, a market move, or a single local storm is not enough to set this band.

levels.name: Bunkered
levels.means: An imminent or unfolding disruption of food, fuel, power, or payments across a large part of the country.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military mobilization order, and it is not a prediction.

levels.name: Full FORTRESS
levels.means: An active nationwide grid-down, or a supply-chain emergency that stops ordinary resupply for most U.S. households. The name is this project's label for that band.
levels.doesNotMean: It is not a military status, a DEFCON level, or a government order. This project does not use an official 90-day threshold from any agency.

checklist.intro: Practical targets for the current band. The basic items come from Ready.gov, the American Red Cross, and CDC water guidance. Buy and rotate what the household will actually use. This is not an order to empty a store.

groups.title: Food
items: About 14 days of foods the household already eats, leaning on items that need no refrigeration and little water to prepare.
A manual can opener.
Foods for infants, special diets, and medical nutrition if someone in the household needs them.
Ready.gov's basic kit is a several-day supply. This level uses the longer Red Cross home window of about two weeks.

groups.title: Water
items: About one gallon per person per day for drinking and sanitation. At this level that is about 14 gallons per person.
More if the climate is hot, someone is ill, or a medical need requires it. Ready.gov notes that needs vary.
Commercially sealed bottles, or food-grade containers kept as Ready.gov describes.
If tap water is unsafe, use bottled water or follow the local health department. CDC explains boiling and other treatment; do not drink water from radiators or boilers.

groups.title: Prescriptions and health
items: The Red Cross basic kit lists a 7-day supply of medications and medical items. This level does not stretch that into a 14-day rule.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before setting aside an emergency supply of prescription medicine. Ready.gov gives the same caution.
A written list of medicines, doses, and allergies, plus glasses and hearing-aid batteries.
A small first-aid kit.

groups.title: Power banks and light
items: A charged phone, its charger, and a backup battery or power bank. Ready.gov includes a backup battery in the basic kit.
A flashlight and spare batteries.
This level does not ask households to buy a generator.

groups.title: Modest cash
items: Small bills.
Enough cash for food, fuel, and a few nights of lodging if card payments do not work. That is the Ready.gov citizen-preparedness guide's framing. This page does not set a dollar amount.

groups.title: Communications
items: A battery-powered or hand-crank radio. A NOAA Weather Radio is useful if you can get one.
A written list of out-of-area contacts, kept with the kit and not only in a phone.
Sign up for the local alert system where you live. This national page cannot do that for you.

groups.title: Accessibility, children, and pets
items: Daily assistive items: extra glasses, hearing-aid batteries, and a plan for devices that need power. Ready.gov's disability guidance says to talk with a clinician about equipment that must stay on.
Infant formula, bottles, and diapers if needed.

Pets: food, water, medicine, a carrier or leash, and ID. Ready.gov says public shelters often refuse pets, so know a place that will take them. If local officials say to evacuate, the pet should go too.
A support network and a paper contact list for anyone who would need help leaving.

methodology: A person reviews this snapshot on a 5-to-1 household scale. Five is the calm end and one is the critical end. The bands match the durations used by the companion household board: several days, about two weeks, about 30 days, about 60 days, and 90 days or more. Those durations are this project's planning labels. They are not agency thresholds. Categories reviewed each time are national energy and grid conditions, supply chains, cyber disruption, weather and disasters, civil disruption, and geopolitical risks that would change U.S. household supplies. Confirmed means the cited page states the fact. Developing means the picture is incomplete, such as a scheduled data gap. Unverified means this review did not confirm it, which is not proof that it is false. Prediction markets and social-media posts are not evidence. The page is a saved assessment with a review time. It is not a live feed, and it does not show a live indicator.
limitations: There is no live feed behind this page. The review time is the time a person last checked the sources.

The petroleum figures are for the week ending November 6, 2026, from EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report released November 12, 2026. Newer weekly figures were not available at the time of this review.
This review did not ingest a live weather, outage, or emergency-declaration map. Local alerts are outside the national number on purpose.
Unverified rows are gaps in the review. They are not findings that a category is calm.
No likelihood percentages, incident timelines, or official trigger values were added where a source did not state them.
Regional stock changes inside the EIA tables already show that a national total can hide opposite local moves.
